newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Ciller stands by Islamists in coalition.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Ciller stands by Islamists in coalition.

text.p: Turkish deputy prime minister Tansu Ciller said on Thursday her conservative True Path Party (DYP) would not abandon its Islamist coalition partners despite a row with the military over the rise of Islamist activity.
"The DYP is not going to hide behind anyone and take part in action to topple the government," Ciller told a party meeting.

Two DYP ministers resigned last weekend in protest at the failure of Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan to act on army demands to curb a revival of religious activity since he came to power last June.
Erbakan, modern Turkey's first Islamist leader, had earlier said he was prepared for early polls if necessary.
But opposition talks on forming an alternative coalition to unseat Erbakan have so far made little progress and main opposition leader Mesut Yilmaz has indicated it is too early for fresh elections.
The military has given Erbakan a list of 18 anti-Islamist measures it wants carried out, including restrictions on Islamist education and enforcement of a ban on Islamic dress.
